title: POV: You Measure the Whole Earth With a Stick (Alexandria, 240 BCE)
hook: With a stick and a shadow, you'll measure the whole Earth.
storyline: Eratosthenes, chief librarian of Alexandria, hears that at midsummer noon in Syene the sun shines straight down a well. The turn: at the same noon, his rod in Alexandria still casts a shadow. One angle and one multiplication later, he has the size of the planet, off by less than one percent.
surprising_fact: Eratosthenes worked out Earth's circumference as about 250,000 stadia, roughly 40,338 km, compared with 40,075 km today. He was off by less than one percent.
voice_direction: Warm, clear, unhurried, about 130 words per minute. Say the numbers slowly. Pause after each sentence. Deliver the last line with quiet pride.

scenes.voice_line: With a stick and a shadow, you'll measure the whole Earth.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: he measured the angle of a rod's shadow at noon on the summer solstice.
Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: he worked in Alexandria in the 3rd century BCE.
Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: he became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.

scenes.voice_line: Down south in Syene, a strange thing happens once a year.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: in Syene at noon on the summer solstice, rods cast no shadows.

scenes.voice_line: Midsummer noon: sunlight falls straight down a well. No shadows.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: the Sun's rays shone straight down into the city-center well.

scenes.voice_line: But here in Alexandria, at that same noon, your rod casts one.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: at noon on the summer solstice there were still shadows in Alexandria.

scenes.voice_line: You measure its angle. One fiftieth of a full circle.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: the shadow's angle was about 7.2 degrees, 1/50 of a full circle.

scenes.voice_line: So Syene must be one fiftieth of the way around.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: the angle between two cities on the same meridian gives their fraction of the circle.

scenes.voice_line: Five thousand stadia between the cities. Times fifty.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: about 5,000 stadia between Alexandria and Syene, multiplied by 50.

scenes.voice_line: Two hundred fifty thousand stadia. About forty thousand kilometres.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: roughly 250,000 stadia, approximately 40,338 km.

scenes.voice_line: A stick, a shadow. Off by less than one percent.
scenes.source_note: Wikipedia, Eratosthenes: about 40,338 km against the modern 40,075.017 km, a difference of about 0.66%.

sources.quote: At noon on the summer solstice, there were still shadows in Alexandria. However, in Syene, rods cast no shadows, and the Sun's rays shone straight down into the city-center well... the shadow's angle to be about 7.2 degrees, which is 1/50 of a full circle... about 5,000 stadia... multiplied this number by 50 and arrived at a total of roughly 250,000 stadia... approximately 40,338 km (25,065 mi), while the modern day measurement... is 40,075.017 km.

description:
Alexandria, about 240 BCE. The chief librarian hears that at midsummer noon the sun shines straight down a well in Syene. At the same moment, his rod in Alexandria still casts a shadow. With one angle and one multiplication he gets the size of the Earth.
